newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem victims' bodies unearthed after four years.
newsitem.headline: Moslem victims' bodies unearthed after four years.

text.p: Government investigators have unearthed bodies of 42 Moslems killed by Serb forces in eastern Bosnia in 1992, a Reuters television team which watched the exhumations reported on Thursday.

The investigators were led to two sites near the town of Ustikolina, 130 km (80 miles) southeast of Sarajevo, by survivors of Serb purges in May of 1992 which killed an unknown number of Moslem residents in three area villages.
"All 42 of these bodies have bullet holes and many had their hands, necks or feet tied with wire," Bosnian investigator Muhidin Niksic told Reuters on Wednesday when the remains were exhumed.
Niksic's team has been digging in the Ustikolina area for the last three weeks and has found a total of 63 bodies.
He suspects another 10 or 15 bodies may be in the area but to recover them the team would need digging machinery.

As investigators pawed through a mud-filled mass grave site near the Drina river with their hands and light tools, human bones and sculls emerged emerged from the muck, tangled with pieces of rotten clothing and wire.
"We also found several scorched bodies in burned houses," Niksic added. "They were all civilians and who had been killed by firearms."

Bosnian forensic experts transported the recovered remains to a make-shift morgue. So far 35 bodies exhumed in the area have been identified by family members or people who saw the executions, Niksic said.
